hero.title: Instagram Reels length limit
hero.lead: A Reel can run up to 20 minutes — the limit rose from 3 minutes during 2025 — but Instagram says Reels longer than 3 minutes get less recommendation reach, so the practical limit for a video you want people to find is still three. Stories are chopped into 60-second segments, and the file itself can be around 4 GB. Length, not size, is what you'll actually bump into.
qa.h2: Instagram video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: Length. A phone recording rarely reaches 4 GB, but a Reel over 3 minutes is shown to fewer people and a Story over 60 seconds is split. Cutting the clip to the moment you want fixes both.
qa.after: Instagram publishes no official size figure, so the 4 GB is best available information; the durations are the ones the app enforces. Because Instagram recompresses everything on upload anyway, there is little to gain from compressing first — trimming is the edit that matters here.
tool.h2: Trim your video to the length you need

fit.r2.q: 3 minutes or less — longer Reels get less reach
fit.after: Limits move often — the Reels ceiling changed twice in 2025 alone. The table above is checked against Instagram's own help pages; the date it was last verified is at the top of this page.
over.p1: Instagram recompresses every upload to its own settings, so shrinking the file first buys you nothing and can cost quality twice over. What helps is cutting: a Reel that opens on the moment and ends before the padding is both under the reach limit and more watchable. For a longer piece, trim it into several Reels or let Stories split it into segments.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. If a file really is huge, the compressor can bring it down while keeping the picture sharp, but for Instagram that's the exception, not the rule.
faq.q1: How long can a Reel be on Instagram?
faq.a1: Up to 20 minutes. Instagram raised the limit from 3 to 20 minutes during 2025, but says Reels longer than 3 minutes are recommended less, so most creators still keep discoverable Reels under three.
faq.q2: Why did Instagram split my Story into pieces?
faq.a2: Stories are limited to 60-second segments. A longer video is cut into consecutive segments automatically. If you'd rather choose the cut yourself, trim the video to the 60 seconds you want first.
faq.q3: Is there a file size limit for Instagram videos?
faq.a3: Instagram doesn't publish one; around 4 GB is the practical ceiling reported for Reels. Phone recordings almost never reach it — length is the limit you'll hit first.
faq.q4: Should I compress my video before uploading to Instagram?
faq.a4: Usually not. Instagram recompresses on upload regardless, so a pre-compressed file just gets compressed again. Upload the best quality you have at the right length; only compress if the file is unusually large or your connection is slow.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I trim it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
